en.title: Job Scheduling
en.description:
Assign m jobs to n processors, with at least one job on each. The numbers of jobs on adjacent processors differ by at most 1. The given k-th processor is the most efficient; find the maximum number of jobs it can get in a valid assignment.

This site added the standard input/output protocol; it does not mean the original function-style problem had this protocol.
en.input: Input n m k, where k is 1-based.
en.output: Output the maximum number of jobs the k-th processor can get.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof, and complexity.
hints: With the peak fixed at x, to minimize the total, the job counts on both sides decrease one by one starting from x−1 and stay at 1 once they reach 1.
